decisions.reason: Connects the top-level ESM import to the boot-composed single classic-script combo: one syntax error aborts whole-combo compilation so zero entries register; typert-registry identified as the first-awaited innocent victim with the culprit in the inner file+position; no blanket claim that ESM is invalid in every context.

Bisects the single new insert row and fully describes the ModuleLoader.load({id, factory}) bundle, package-name id, host React via factory require, and apply/inject exports; but diagnosis relies on a top-level import/export grep, never parsing the bundle as a classic script (no vm.Script-equivalent) and not addressing node --check's insufficiency.

Correctly establishes declaration ownership and the declarant/registrant field split (no kind/scope from the registrant), but shows only an immediate ctx.slots.inject(slot, {descriptor}) form (admittedly inferred), not the deferred register-callback form that waits for the declaration, and never establishes that cross-entry apply ordering is unguaranteed.

Combo assembled once per boot with no watcher, so every edit needs a full restart; Windows process-tree kill (taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F) for the orphan; EADDRINUSE explained as the old process retaining the port, not a packaging defect; refresh and plugin-list verification included.

Host side: per-bundle isolated classic-contract validation with plugin-id/position attribution instead of the first-awaited entry, plus per-entry isolation; author side: checklist covering loader factory, host React via require, inject/apply exports, inject-not-register slot rule, and the restart/tree-kill dev loop.

caps.reason: Final advice mandates the loader wrapper, slots.inject contribution, registrant-only fields, and host restarts over refresh; none of the capped bad recommendations is affirmed.
